title: Probability and statistics
targetPerformance: By hour 20, solve at least 16 of 20 fresh counting, conditional-probability, expectation, binomial, and z-score tasks in 45 minutes; explain a sampling-distribution prediction and build a reproducible simulation that passes its tests.
whyItMatters: Distinguish chance variation from evidence and check uncertain claims against explicit sample spaces.

subskills.title: Count the sample space
subskills.why: Choose whether order and replacement matter.
subskills.selfCorrection: List a tiny example before choosing a counting formula.

subskills.title: Probability rules
subskills.selfCorrection: Keep probabilities in [0,1] and subtract overlap once.
drills: Use a complement for at least one.

subskills.title: Conditional probability and Bayes
subskills.why: Shrink the sample space to the evidence.
subskills.selfCorrection: State the conditioning group and include base rates.

subskills.title: Expectation and variance
subskills.selfCorrection: Check variance is nonnegative and has squared units.
drills: Use E(X squared) minus E(X) squared.

subskills.title: Binomial models
subskills.why: Count successes in independent fixed trials.
subskills.selfCorrection: Check fixed n, common p, and independence before applying the model.

subskills.title: Normal distribution and z-scores
subskills.selfCorrection: Check the sign of x minus mean and distinguish SD from variance.
drills: Use symmetry and the standard normal CDF.

subskills.title: Sampling and CLT
subskills.why: Distinguish a population from means of samples.
subskills.selfCorrection: Check independence and divide SD by sqrt(n), not n.
drills: Predict spread as sample size grows.
Compare raw observations and sample means.

subskills.title: Simulation and model checks
subskills.why: Compare long-run experiments with exact predictions.
subskills.selfCorrection: Use a fixed local random seed and compare with analytic scale.

resources.title: Seeing Theory
resources.why: Interactive views of probability, distributions, and sampling; use it to check a prediction visually.

resources.title: Khan Academy — Statistics and probability
resources.why: Short videos and instantly checked exercises for counting, conditional probability, and z-scores.

resources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
resources.why: Free worked examples for probability and introductory inference.

resources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare — 18.05 Introduction to Probability and Statistics
resources.why: Reading questions and problem sets with solutions for Bayes, expectation, and the CLT.

barriers.fix: Attempt one prompt before consulting one short resource section.
Sketch or describe the quantities, predict sign and scale, then compute.
Record the failed assumption, use the next hint, and retry with changed numbers.
